the formalization of the knowledge associated to NFRs in software design.
the formalization of the knowledge on design patterns and NFRs in a fuzzy ontology and with the development of a tool to support the decision making process of architectural solutions.
the design of a tool that supports the architectural design process by providing a ranked list of design patterns that satisfy the NFRs specified by the designer.

the proposed approach is an innovative and effective tool to support the decision making process in software architectural design.

the approach presented in this paper allows designers to take into account non functional requirements in their architectural design decisions, by providing a ranked set of patterns able to satisfy the specified NFRs.
the proposed approach allows the designer to retrieve, in a tool supported way, a ranked list of architectural design pattern sets able to fulfill the non functional requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed approach is able to provide a tool-supported decision making procedure for the architectural design of a software system, based on a fuzzy ontology that encodes the relations and interactions among NFRs and patterns.
we provide a formal framework to model and reason over NFRs in software architecture design, and to retrieve a ranked set of patterns able to satisfy the NFRs.
we propose an innovative approach to model the knowledge on N FRs and to support their exploitation in the software architectural design.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a formalization of NFRs and the mutual relations among them, together with the possibility of reasoning over them in a declarative way, can be a valuable tool for designers and architects to make decisions about architectural solutions.

the proposed fuzzy ontology based approach is able to model the mutual relations among NFRs and patterns, thus enabling a decision making process that is able to take into account the NFRs during the software architecture design.
we provide a formal framework for the representation of NFRs, which can support the decision making process in the software design.
